subject: serializing stan models under R, platform windows

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: serializing stan models under R, platform windows
parts:
Hi!

I am trying to provide a binary R library on a windows platform. So I serialized my stan model in question with

sm1 <- stan("log2bayes_single.stan", chains=0, data=NULL)
saveRDS(sm1, "log2bayes_single.rda")

and on the target machine I intended to run the code

l2b_fit <- readRDS("log2bayes_single.rda")
l2b <- stan(fit=l2b_fit, warmup=250, iter=1250)

However, this works on my own machine, but on the target machine this crashes R horribly with the message

"Error in withCallingHandlers(tryCatch ...
object '.rcpp_warning_recorder' not found

I would prefer not to rely on the auto_write feature and make calls ala stan("log2bayes_single.stan") while assuming that the auto_write stuff will take care of it. On the target machines, there will be no Rtools installed, only rstan; hence this model caching must work.

I would prefer to use rstan, but a solution could be to stick to cmdstan binaries. Or could during the package building a compile step of the C++ translated stan model be integrated?

Many thanks for any pointers.

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: serializing stan models under R, platform windows
parts:
On Thursday, July 30, 2015 at 9:14:05 AM UTC-4, Sebastian Weber wrote:
I would prefer not to rely on the auto_write feature and make calls ala stan("log2bayes_single.stan") while assuming that the auto_write stuff will take care of it. On the target machines, there will be no Rtools installed, only rstan; hence this model caching must work.

The serialization and deserialization of compiled code won't work across platforms. It might work if you compiled the model on a Windows machine with Rtools but only if the other machine had the same bitness.

Ben
